reasons: The file depends on a data file that is not visible here.
Matching of questions is exact after normalising, so small rewording gets no answer.

terms.meaning: A plain text format for structured data, here the storyline file.
A label the app uses to store and look up fetched data in memory.
To tidy text for comparison, such as lowercasing it and removing punctuation.
Data that can be viewed but not changed.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the storyline
sections.what: Loads the recorded storyline file and brings in the base web address, the search result type and the filter type.
sections.why: Setup code. It supplies the data and types the storyline uses.
sections.watch_out: The storyline JSON file must exist beside this file at build time, or the demo will not build.

sections.name: RecordedAsk
sections.title: Recorded question and answer
sections.what: Describes the prepared AI question: its text, when it was captured, which model produced it, whether it is a keyword placeholder, which signals it covers, and the result.
sections.why: Gives the demo one fixed question with a fixed answer, since no model runs in the demo.
sections.watch_out: The placeholder flag tells visitors the answer is not from a model, so it must stay accurate when the answer is recorded.

sections.name: Storyline, OM_DEMO_STATE_KEY, pinsWith, fmtDay, norm
sections.title: Storyline definition and small helpers
sections.what: Defines the full storyline shape: title, pinned date, filters, sort, view, signal list with roles, pinned account, profile, and the prepared question. It also sets the demo and live web addresses, the separate demo cache key, a role lookup, a date formatter, and a text normaliser.
sections.why: Likely reason: the separate cache key keeps demo edits from reaching live data. The date formatter adds noon time to plain dates, which avoids showing the wrong day in some time zones; the code does not state this.
sections.watch_out: The demo must keep its own cache key. Using the live key would let demo changes leak into the real workspace.

sections.name: recordedAnswer
sections.title: Matching the prepared question
sections.what: Returns the recorded answer only when the typed question matches the prepared one after ignoring case and punctuation. Any other question returns nothing.
sections.why: Matches the demo rule that only the prepared question gets an answer.
sections.watch_out: Any rewording of the prepared question gets no answer, which is intended for the demo.

summary: Loads the recorded LNG storyline used by the Opportunity Map demo and provides the fixed question-and-answer lookup and the demo's separate storage key.
purpose: Holds the example that the demo shows, so visitors see a stable, repeatable walkthrough of real saved data.
why: Likely reason: a fixed example lets the demo be repeatable and read-only. The file header says the demo reads saved data through normal read endpoints only.
how: 1. Loads the storyline JSON file. 2. Defines the type that describes its contents. 3. Exports the story, the demo and live web addresses, and a separate cache key. 4. Provides a helper to list signal ids by role, a date formatter, and a text normaliser. 5. recordedAnswer returns the recorded answer only when the typed question matches the prepared one.
inputs: The storyline JSON file beside it, and the user's typed question when asked.
outputs: The storyline object, addresses and cache key used by other demo files, and a recorded answer or nothing.
risks: If the JSON file is missing or does not match the type, the demo breaks. The recorded answer may be a keyword placeholder rather than a model answer, which is flagged in the data.
debug: If the demo will not load, check that lng-storyline.json exists and is valid. If a question gets no answer, check the prepared question text and that the answer result is present. If demo edits appear in the live workspace, check that the demo cache key is used.
